 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.07.2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.1358/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, SRIRANGAPATNA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants-appellants, challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1358/2011 dated 05.07.2014 by the Court of Additional Senior Civil Judge, MACT,
Srirangapatna, seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text:
Court of Additional Senior Civil Judge, MACT,
Srirangapatna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 18.11.2007 at about 4.30 p.m., deceased Virupaksha was riding his motor bike bearing registration No.KA-11-Q- 8742 from Mahadeshwara Hills to Srirangapatna.

When the deceased Virupaksha along with his relative Ramesh was riding on the left side of the road near Saragoor lake on Kollegala, Mahadeshwara Hills Main Road, the driver of goods lorry bearing registration No.TN-39-AP-1771 driven the same from opposite direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor bike, as a result of which, Virupaksha and Ramesh fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Virupaksha succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.
The claimants being the wife, daughter and mother of deceased Virupaksha have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.

sentences.text:
4. The Tribunal after considering oral and documentary evidence on record, has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,06,000/- under different heads, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, as follows:
Sl.

No . Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Loss of dependency 5,76,000-00 2. Loss of consortium 10,000-00 3. Loss of estate, love and 10,000-00 affection 4.
Funeral expenses 10,000-00 Total 6,06,000-00
5. Being aggrieved by the lesser quantum of compensation, the present appeal is filed.

6. In the present case, the deceased was aged about 35 years, he was an agriculturist,
earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Even though the Tribunal has correctly taken the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month, but not added loss of future prospects in life.
Therefore, the same needs to be modified.
The accident is of the year 2007.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.4,500/- p.m., as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

It is just and proper to add 40% of the income towards future prospects, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 2700.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are three dependants.
Hence, 1/3rd of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenditure.
The appropriate multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.
Therefore, the 'Loss of Dependency' would be re-
assessed and quantified as under:

Rs.4,500 + Rs.1,800 (40% of Rs.4,500) = Rs.6,300/- Rs.6,300 x 2/3 x 16 x 12 =
Rs.8,06,400/- Accordingly, a sum of Rs.8,06,400/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
each towards 'Loss of consortium' 'Loss of estate' and 'Loss of love and affection', which is on the lesser side.
The loss of consortium and loss of love and affection are more or less having the same connotations.
The claimants are the wife, daughter and mother of the deceased.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000/- each) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium' as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782.

sentences.text: The cost incurred on account of 'Transportation of dead body, funeral and ritual expenses' and towards 'loss of estate' is modified by granting a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the said heads.

9. Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.9,56,400/- under the following heads :
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  01 Loss of dependency 8,06,400-00
02 Loss of consortium 1,20,000-00
03 Transportation of dead 15,000-00  body, funeral & ritual  expenses  04 Loss of estate 15,000-00  TOTAL COMPENSATION Rs.9,56,400-00 10.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.6,06,000/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.9,56,400/-.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,50,400/- (Rs.9,56,400 - Rs.6,06,000) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

11. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1358/2011 dated 05.07.2014 by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Srirangapatha, is hereby modified and appellants/claimants are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,50,400/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Ordered accordingly.
